rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl, who threatened the Prophet for praying at the House.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل ، لعنه الله ، توعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الصلاة عند البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forbidding man is challenged to consider what if the person he stops is acting on a straight path.
rows.anchor: فما ظنك إن كان هذا الذي تنهاه على الطريق المستقيمة في فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person being stopped may be urging God-fearing conduct in speech while the forbidding man threatens him over prayer.
rows.anchor: أو { أَمَرَ بِالتَّقْوَى } بقوله ، وأنت تزجره وتتوعده على صلاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forbidding man should know that God sees him, hears his words, and will recompense him fully.
rows.anchor: أن الله يراه ويسمع كلامه ، وسيجازيه على فعله أتم الجزاء

rows.anchor: أن الله يراه ويسمع كلامه ، وسيجازيه على فعله أتم الجزاء

words: كَلَّا لَئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًۢا بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Abu Jahl does not stop his dissension and obstinacy, God threatens to blacken his forelock on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: لئن لم يرجع عما هو فيه من الشقاق والعناد { لَنَسْفَعَنْ بِالنَّاصِيَةِ } أي : لنَسمَنَّها سوادا يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forelock belongs to Abu Jahl: it is false in its speech and sinful in its deeds.
rows.anchor: ناصية أبي جهل كاذبة في مقالها خاطئة في فعَالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The council is the man's people and clan, whom he is challenged to call for support.
rows.anchor: أي : قومه وعشيرته ، أي : ليدعهم يستنصر بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zabāniya are the angels of punishment; the contest will show whether God's party or Abu Jahl's party prevails.
rows.anchor: وهم ملائكة العذاب ، حتى يعلم من يغلب : أحزبنا أو حزبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl's threat to trample the Prophet's neck at the Kaaba; the Prophet warned that angels would seize him if he did.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قال أبو جهل : لئن رأيت محمدا يصلي عند الكعبة لأطأن على عنقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another Ibn Abbas report, Abu Jahl threatens the Prophet at the Maqam and boasts of his large council; Ibn Abbas says angels would seize the council immediately. Al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام فمر به أبو جهل بن هشام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits Abu Jahl's threat to step on the Prophet's neck; the Prophet says angels would seize him in plain sight, then mentions the fate of Jews wishing for death and those who left for mutual imprecation.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال أبو جهل : لئن رأيت رسول الله يصلي عند الكعبة لآتينه حتى أطأ على عنقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A further Ibn Abbas version says Abu Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad at the Maqam; revelation followed, and Abu Jahl saw battalions between them. Ibn Abbas says angels would seize him if he moved.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال أبو جهل : لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl recoiled from the praying Prophet, seeing a fiery trench, dread, and wings; the Prophet said angels would seize him limb by limb.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir is unsure whether Abu Hurayra's report itself says that the passage from 96:6 through the end of the sura was revealed.
rows.anchor: وأنزل الله - لا أدري في حديث أبي هريرة أم لا - :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad must not obey the command to stop abundant, continual worship; he may pray wherever he wishes without concern because God protects and supports him.
rows.anchor: لا تطعه فيما ينهاك عنه من المداومة على العبادة وكثرتها ، وصل حيث شئت ولا تباله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating, so worshippers should make abundant supplication.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir recalls that the Prophet prostrated when reciting al-Inshiqaq and Iqra.
rows.anchor: وتقدم أيضا : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This statement is the object of the preceding oath: humanity is ungrateful and denies its Lord's blessings.
rows.anchor: هذا هو المقسم عليه ، بمعنى أنه لنعم ربه لجحود كفور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وإبراهيم النخعي، وأبو الجوزاء، وأبو العالية، وأبو الضحى، وسعيد بن جبير، ومحمد بن قيس، والضحاك، والحسن، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وابن زيد
rows.claim: These authorities gloss kanūd as intensely ungrateful or disbelieving toward God's blessings.
rows.anchor: الربيع بن أنس ، وابن زيد : الكنود : الكفور

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the ungrateful person keeps count of misfortunes and forgets his Lord's blessings.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : هو الذي يعد المصائب ، وينسى نعم ربه

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Umamah calls the kanūd person ungrateful, eating alone, beating his servant, and withholding help; Ibn Kathir calls its marfuʿ chain weak because Jaʿfar b. al-Zubayr is abandoned, and notes al-Tabari's mawquf version.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-khayr means wealth; one view is that the person intensely loves wealth, which Ibn Kathir accepts along with the second view.
rows.anchor: أي : وإنه لحب الخير - وهو : المال - لشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other valid view is that love of wealth makes the person greedy and miserly.
rows.anchor: والثاني : وإنه لحريص بخيل ؛ من محبة المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies Surat al-Asr as Meccan.
rows.anchor: تفسير سورة العصر ، وهي مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report places Amr b. al-As with Musaylima after Muhammad's mission but before Amr's conversion: Musaylima asks what was revealed, Amr recites al-Asr, Musaylima offers nonsense verse, and Amr calls him a liar.
rows.anchor: ذكروا أن عمرو بن العاص وفد على مسيلمة الكذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says he saw Abu Bakr al-Khara'iti transmit this story, or something close to it, in the second part of his Maʿāyib al-Akhlāq.
rows.anchor: وقد رأيت أبا بكر الخرائطي أسند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wabr is a small animal resembling a cat, notable for its large ears and chest and ugly in the rest of its body.
rows.anchor: والوبْر : دويبة تشبه الهر ، أعظم شيء فيه أذناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musaylima fashioned this gibberish to rival the Qur'an, but even a pagan worshipper of idols was not taken in by it.
rows.anchor: فأراد مسيلمة أن يركب من هذا الهذيان ما يعارض به القرآن ، فلم يرج ذلك على عابد الأوثان في ذلك الزمان

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن حصن أبو مدينة
rows.claim: Al-Tabarani reports from Abu Madinah that two Companions who met would not part until one recited the whole sura to the other, then they exchanged greetings.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن حصن[ أبي مدينة ] ، قال

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi says that if people reflected on this sura, it would suffice them.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي ، رحمه الله : لو تدبر الناس هذه السورة ، لوسعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-asr is the span of time in which human actions occur, whether good or evil.
rows.anchor: العصر : الزمان الذي يقع فيه حركات بني آدم ، من خير وشر

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Malik transmits Zayd b. Aslam's interpretation of al-asr as the late afternoon or evening.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك ، عن زيد بن أسلم : هو العشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the famous interpretation is the first one: time in general, rather than evening alone.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك ، عن زيد بن أسلم : هو العشي ، والمشهور الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception consists of those who believe in their hearts and perform righteous deeds with their limbs.
rows.anchor: فاستثنى من جنس الإنسان عن الخسران الذين آمنوا بقلوبهم ، وعملوا الصالحات بجوارحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual counsel in truth means carrying out acts of obedience and leaving prohibited acts.
rows.anchor: وهو أداء الطاعات ، وترك المحرمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual counsel in patience applies to calamities, decrees, and the harm of those whom believers command to do right and forbid from wrong.
rows.anchor: على المصائب والأقدار ، وأذى من يؤذي ممن يأمرونه بالمعروف وينهونه عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies Surat al-Maʿun as Meccan.
rows.anchor: تفسير السورة التي يذكر فيها الماعون وهي مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-din here means resurrection, reckoning, and recompense.
rows.anchor: يكذب بالدين ؟ وهو : المعاد والجزاء والثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He forcefully oppresses the orphan and withholds the orphan's due, neither feeding nor treating him well.
rows.anchor: هو الذي يقهر اليتيم ويظلمه حقه ، ولا يطعمه ولا يحسن إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means those committed to prayer who are nevertheless heedless of it.
rows.anchor: أي : الذين هم من أهل الصلاة وقد التزموا بها ، ثم هم عنها ساهون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say these are hypocrites who pray publicly but do not pray in private.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ، وغيره : يعني المنافقين ، الذين يصلون في العلانية ولا يصلون في السر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes heedlessness to include abandoning prayer altogether.
rows.anchor: عن فعلها بالكلية ، كما قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مسروق وأبو الضحى
rows.claim: Masruq and Abu al-Duha interpret it as failing to perform prayer within its legally prescribed time.
rows.anchor: في الوقت المقدر لها شرعا ، فيخرجها عن وقتها بالكلية ، كما قاله مسروق ، وأبو الضحى

rows.speaker: عطاء بن دينار
rows.claim: Ataa b. Dinar notes that the verse says heedless about their prayer, not heedless within prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء بن دينار : والحمد لله الذي قال : { عَنْ صَلاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ } ولم يقل : في صلاتهم ساهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another form is habitual delay from the prayer's first time until its end.
rows.anchor: وإما عن وقتها الأول فيؤخرونها إلى آخره دائما أو غالبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase also covers failing to perform prayer with its commanded pillars and conditions.
rows.anchor: وإما عن أدائها بأركانها وشروطها على الوجه المأمور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also covers lack of reverence in prayer and reflection on its meanings.
rows.anchor: وإما عن الخشوع فيها والتدبر لمعانيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording includes all these forms; anyone with one has a share of the verse, while someone with all completes his share and practical hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: فاللفظ يشمل هذا كله ، ولكل من اتصف بشيء من ذلك قسط من هذه الآية

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls the prayer of a hypocrite one repeated three times: he waits for the sun to near the devil's horns, then pecks out four units with little remembrance.
rows.anchor: كما ثبت في الصحيحين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies this as the middle prayer, Asr, delayed to its last and disliked time; the worshipper then pecks like a crow without composure or reverence.
rows.anchor: فهذا آخر صلاة العصر التي هي الوسطى ، كما ثبت به النص إلى آخر وقتها ، وهو وقت كراهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir suspects that ostentation, rather than seeking God's favor, motivated the hypocrite to pray, so in effect he had not prayed at all.
rows.anchor: ولعله إنما حمله على القيام إليها مراءاة الناس ، لا ابتغاء وجه الله ، فهو إذًا لم يصل بالكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the hypocrites' lazy, showy prayer and scant remembrance to the description of hypocrites in 4:142.
rows.anchor: ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا } [ النساء : 142 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He points forward to the following description of those who show off.
rows.anchor: وقال هاهنا : { الَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَاءُونَ }

rows.claim: He points forward to the following description of those who show off.
rows.anchor: وقال هاهنا : { الَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَاءُونَ }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophet's account of a valley in Hell that Hell seeks refuge from 400 times daily, prepared for show-offs including Qur'an reciters, givers, pilgrims, and those who go out in God's path.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever publicizes deeds for people will have God publicize him among creation and humiliate him; Ahmad gives another route through an unnamed man.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن عمرو يقول : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak remarks, after the Abu Hurayra report about public notice, that it is a good hadith for show-offs.
rows.anchor: بلغني أن ابن المبارك قال : نعم الحديث للمرائين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An act done for God does not become ostentation merely because people see it and the doer feels pleased by that.
rows.anchor: أن من عمل عملا لله فاطلع عليه الناس ، فأعجبه ذلك ، أن هذا لا يعد رياء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says the Prophet promised two rewards, for secret and public worship, when a man who had prayed privately was pleased that a visitor saw him; Ibn Kathir calls this route gharib, rates Saʿid b. Bashir middling, and says his report from al-Aʿmash is rare though others also transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : كنت أصلي ، فدخل علي رجل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A second Abu Hurayra report gives the same two rewards; al-Tirmidhi calls it gharib and notes that al-Aʿmash and others also transmit the report from Habib as mursal.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In Abu Barza's report, the Prophet says the heedless person who expects no good from prayer and fears no Lord when abandoning it is worse off than receiving the whole world; the chain is weak because Jabir al-Juʿfi is weak and his teacher unnamed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي برزة الأسلمي قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Saʿd b. Abi Waqqas asks about the heedless; the Prophet answers that they delay prayer beyond its time. The raised route is weakened, while the mawquf report from Saʿd is more sound and was authenticated by al-Bayhaqi and al-Hakim.
rows.anchor: عن مصعب بن سعد ، عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال : سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Delaying prayer beyond its time may mean abandoning it, praying after its legally set time, or postponing it from its first time until the time expires.
rows.anchor: يحتمل تركها بالكلية ، أو صلاتها بعد وقتها شرعا
